exceptions.justification: The move from a repository-root disable-comments.json to .repo-contract/exceptions/disable-comments.json is a one-time `git mv` in the same commit -- the file's content, bare-array shape, and every field are unchanged, and a full `npm run contract` run confirms zero synchronization drift (0 new / 0 moved / 0 removed) against the new location. scripts/suppression-governance/ is a self-hosting check, never part of the published package (package.json `files`), so no external consumer ever runs it against a legacy layout. The failure mode the finding describes -- an absent new file beside a stale root file causing a silent empty-registry synthesis -- is a transient state only an unrebased branch or a stale local checkout hits for a single merge, and an ordinary merge conflict on the relocated file surfaces it. A permanent legacy-import plus dual-path-precedence code path would be dead weight the moment this transition completes, against this repository's standing preference for fewer special cases in the suppression-governance flow (see specs/decisions/0006-suppression-governance.md and the disable-comments.json fragility notes).
exceptions.remediation: None planned. A local checkout that somehow retains only a root disable-comments.json is repaired with `git mv disable-comments.json .repo-contract/exceptions/disable-comments.json`; ADR 0006's Status section records the move and its rationale. Revisit only if suppression-governance is ever promoted to a consumer-facing surface, at which point a real migration path (import + precedence + upgrade-path test) would be warranted.

verification.evidence: CodeRabbit local review on branch feat/move-disable-comments-to-exceptions-dir (2026-09-08); the migration-path finding was reviewed and accepted by the maintainer as a one-time git-mv migration that needs no code.
